note: Written with caveats. The supplement states "All questions below used a 1–6 Likert scale (1=strongly disagree; 6=strongly agree)", but the deposited data (and the live IRW table) hold only 1-5 on all 22 items: 37,818 responses, zero 6s (counts 1=1464, 2=3956, 3=8506, 4=16973, 5=6919). The paper's own domain alphas reproduce exactly from this 1-5 file, so it is the analysed data; the 2009 MedSEQ synopsis (unsworks 10.26190/unsworks/623) describes the pre-2017 version with a 5-point 'only rarely'..'almost always' frequency scale and different items, so it does not settle the 2017 anchors. option_text is therefore left blank for all five levels rather than guessed. Step 5b: per-domain Cronbach's alpha recomputed from live data under the supplement's Q-number->domain assignment reproduces 7 of 8 published values to 3 decimals (teaching 1-3 0.719/0.719, assessment 4-6 0.833/0.833, staff 7-9 0.850/0.850, learning 10-13 0.856/0.856, clinical 14-15 0.708/0.708, online 16-17 0.687/0.687, cultural 18-19 0.712/0.712); being cared for (20-22) gives 0.661 vs published 0.749, and no contiguous or content-plausible item set gives 0.749, so 20-22 is assigned by elimination and the 0.749 treated as a source-side discrepancy. Shifting all items by +/-1 matches 0/8 domains (max dev 0.259/0.271). Order within each domain is not established. Q_Satisfaction (item 23, 4-point) is a covariate in the IRW table, not an item, so its wording is not shipped. Rights: MedSEQ is UNSW's in-house instrument; wording taken from the study's own CC BY 4.0 paper supplement on a CC0 Dataverse deposit; no restriction on the instrument located or quoted; no register row.

PASS with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the paper states "The IGDS9-SF, GDT, and BSMAS were translated into the Bengali (participants' first language)" using a conceptual (not literal) forward-backward translation, but no Bengali wording is recoverable in scope: S1 File (journal.pone.0279062.s001.xlsx, CC BY) has bare headers BSMAS1..BSMAS6 and zero Bengali-script characters; S2 File (s002.docx, correlation tables), S3 (s003.docx, peer review) and S4 (s004.docx, response to reviewers) contain zero Bengali-script characters; the article XML contains zero Bengali-script characters and prints no BSMAS item stems (only the anchors 1 'very rarely' to 5 'very often'). So canonical English BSMAS wording ships in the base fields, language=Bengali, _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute. (2) MAPPING IS BY CANONICAL NUMBERING, NOT A SOURCE LABEL: data/islam_2022_online_addiction.py takes item codes verbatim from the S1 headers (derivation pattern 1, no positional step), but those headers carry no text, and the paper's tables (Table 1 descriptives, Table 5 loadings) are keyed to the same bare codes. BSMASK is assigned canonical BSMAS item K. Step 5b (verify_islam_2022_bsmas.R) confirms the codes are the paper's own (Table 1 mean/SD reproduce to <=0.0005, each item nearest its own published row) and the scale direction (BSMAS total vs internet hours r=0.224 live vs 0.225 published), but no route ties a code to a wording -- status PARTIAL. (3) TWO ENGLISH RENDERINGS circulate (interrogative 'How often during the last year have you...' and declarative 'You spend a lot of time...', the latter on the Salford PsyTech page). The interrogative form is shipped, matching the corpus precedent ma2026_bsmas (batch_092); which rendering the Bengali translation was made from is not recorded. Leading item numbers and ellipses ('1. ...') of the source table were stripped; the stem is in instructions with the source's own ellipsis character. Middle anchors (rarely/sometimes/often) come from the canonical instrument; the study paper prints only the two endpoints. (4) Item 6's canonical 'your job/studies' reflects the original scale; respondents were school-going adolescents. (5) RIGHTS: register row 'Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS)' verdict=ship (attribution only: Salford PsyTech 'Ensure you cite the author(s).'); applied, not re-derived. Wording copied from Ozimek et al. 2025, Behav Sci 15(12):1719, PMC12729781, CC BY 4.0. (6) Step 3b OK: live table is 6 items, resp 1-5, per-item means match the paper's BSMAS rows in Table 1 -- it is the BSMAS, not the sibling IGDS9-SF/GDT/PHQ-9/GAD-7 in the same file.
